clinician.trajectory_summary: A 12-year-old male presented to the Emergency Room at Kassala Teaching Hospital, Sudan with convulsions, headache, and high-grade fever. Non-contrast CT imaging revealed two critical intracranial lesions: (1) a 5.7 × 4.7 × 5.3 cm right frontal peripherally enhancing cystic lesion with vasogenic edema and 1.5 cm midline shift consistent with brain abscess, and (2) an avidly enhancing lesion within the third ventricle in continuation with the straight sinus, surrounded by extensive vascular loops consistent with a vein of Galen aneurysm. The aneurysm caused compression of the cerebral aqueduct, resulting in mild hydrocephalus with dilation of both lateral ventricles. The combined mass effect from the abscess and aneurysm created significant raised intracranial pressure. The patient received no further treatment and died 2 hours after the imaging procedures, with death attributed to the severe intracranial pathology and elevated intracranial pressure.
